classification.difficultyReason: Convert mixed hours and minutes into a single time unit before dividing distance by time. This links a routine unit conversion with the average-speed calculation.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A plane travels 2000 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is the average speed of the plane?

answer.worked:
$2\text{ hours }30\text{ minutes}=2\frac12\text{ hours}=\frac52\text{ hours}$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{\text{distance travelled}}{\text{time taken}}\\\text{Average speed}&=2000\div\frac52\\\text{Average speed}&=2000\times\frac25\\\text{Average speed}&=800\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A car travels 200 km in 1 hour 50 minutes. What is the average speed of the car? Give your answer in kilometres per hour (km/h), correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
$1\text{ hour }50\text{ minutes}=1\frac56\text{ hours}=\frac{11}{6}\text{ hours}$.

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{\text{distance travelled}}{\text{time taken}}\\\text{Average speed}&=200\div\frac{11}{6}\\\text{Average speed}&=200\times\frac6{11}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{1200}{11}\text{ km/h}\\\text{Average speed}&=109\frac1{11}\text{ km/h}\\\text{Average speed}&\approx109.1\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$
